source.subject: Biology
source.unit: Unit 1 — Diversity in the Living World
source.source_scope: Only the content printed on PDF page 6 (printed page 15): Sections 2.2.2 Dinoflagellates, 2.2.3 Euglenoids, 2.2.4 Slime Moulds, the start of 2.2.5 Protozoans (introduction and amoeboid protozoans), and Figure 2.4.

questions.question: Dinoflagellates are mostly:
questions.explanation: The page says dinoflagellates are mostly marine and photosynthetic.
questions.source_text: These organisms are mostly marine and photosynthetic.

questions.question: Dinoflagellates appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on:
options: The main pigments present in their cells
The thickness of their cell wall
questions.explanation: The page says the colour depends on the main pigments present in the cells.
questions.source_text: They appear yellow, green, brown, blue or red depending on the main pigments present in their cells.

questions.question: The cell wall of dinoflagellates has on its outer surface:
questions.explanation: The page says the cell wall has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.
questions.source_text: The cell wall has stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.

questions.question: Most dinoflagellates have two flagella. How are they arranged?
options: One short and one long, both at the anterior end
Many flagella cover the whole surface
One lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates
Both lie longitudinally at the posterior end
questions.explanation: The page describes one longitudinal and one transverse flagellum lying in a furrow between the wall plates.
questions.source_text: one lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates.

questions.question: Red tides are caused by rapid multiplication of:
questions.explanation: The page says red dinoflagellates (example Gonyaulax) multiply so rapidly that they make the sea appear red.
questions.source_text: red dinoflagellates (Example: Gonyaulax) undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red (red tides).

questions.question: Toxins released by large numbers of red dinoflagellates may:
options: Kill other marine animals such as fishes
questions.explanation: The page says the toxins released by such large numbers may even kill other marine animals such as fishes.
questions.source_text: Toxins released by such large numbers may even kill other marine animals such as fishes.

questions.question: Most euglenoids are found in:
questions.explanation: The page says the majority are fresh water organisms found in stagnant water.
questions.source_text: Majority of them are fresh water organisms found in stagnant water.

questions.question: Instead of a cell wall, euglenoids have a protein-rich layer called:
questions.explanation: The page says the protein-rich pellicle makes the body of euglenoids flexible.
questions.source_text: they have a protein rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.

questions.question: Euglenoids have two flagella, which are:
options: One longitudinal and one transverse in a furrow
questions.explanation: The page says euglenoids have two flagella, a short and a long one.
questions.source_text: They have two flagella, a short and a long one.

questions.question: When deprived of sunlight, euglenoids behave like heterotrophs by:
questions.explanation: The page says that without sunlight euglenoids behave like heterotrophs by predating on other smaller organisms.
questions.source_text: when deprived of sunlight they behave like heterotrophs by predating on other smaller organisms.

questions.question: The pigments of euglenoids are identical to those present in:
questions.explanation: The page notes that the pigments of euglenoids are identical to those in higher plants.
questions.source_text: the pigments of euglenoids are identical to those present in higher plants.

questions.question: Slime moulds are:
questions.explanation: The page says slime moulds are saprophytic protists.

questions.question: Under suitable conditions, slime moulds form an aggregation called:
questions.explanation: The page says the aggregation called plasmodium may grow and spread over several feet.
questions.source_text: they form an aggregation called plasmodium which may grow and spread over several feet.

questions.question: Which statements about slime mould spores are correct?
options: They are extremely resistant and can survive for many years
They are dispersed by air currents
They are borne in fruiting bodies at the tips of the differentiated plasmodium
They are dispersed only by water
questions.explanation: The page describes the spores as borne at the tips of fruiting bodies, with true walls, very resistant, surviving many years and dispersed by air currents.
questions.source_text: the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips. The spores possess true walls. They are extremely resistant and survive for many years

questions.question: All protozoans are:
options: Heterotrophs living as predators or parasites
questions.explanation: The page says all protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites.
questions.source_text: All protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites.

questions.question: Protozoans are believed to be primitive relatives of:
questions.explanation: The page says protozoans are believed to be primitive relatives of animals.
questions.source_text: They are believed to be primitive relatives of animals.

questions.question: Into how many major groups are protozoans divided on the page?
questions.explanation: The page says there are four major groups of protozoans.
questions.source_text: There are four major groups of protozoans.

questions.question: Match each protist group with a characteristic from this page.
questions.explanation: Red tides are linked to dinoflagellates, the pellicle to euglenoids, the plasmodium to slime moulds and predation or parasitism to protozoans.
questions.source_text: make the sea appear red (red tides). ... a protein rich layer called pellicle ... they form an aggregation called plasmodium ... live as predators or parasites.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Euglenoids are always photosynthetic, whatever the light conditions.
Reason (R): The pigments of euglenoids are identical to those present in higher plants.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: A is false because euglenoids behave like heterotrophs when deprived of sunlight. R is true as stated on the page.
questions.source_text: Though they are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight, when deprived of sunlight they behave like heterotrophs
